business_scope.primary_industry_name: Fitness Biometric Tracking and Wellness Telemetry Apps

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 (ss. 2-19, incorporation; s. 110, registered office; s. 142, directors; s. 168, secretary) read with the Income Tax Act 2010 exemption regime; Companies (Fees) Regulations 2022; Companies (Continuation) Regulations 2015 (if preserving the Bermuda Exempted Co. shell by redomiciliation).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Gibraltar Registrar of Companies (Companies House), Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC), Line Wall Road, Gibraltar.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form CO-01 (Application for Certificate of Incorporation) accompanied by the Memorandum and Articles of Association and statutory declarations of compliance.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital required; company may incorporate with nil paid or nominal par-value shares. No escrow account or capital deposit mandate applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED as the First Board Resolution, adopted in writing pursuant to the Articles of Association: (1) the company accepts the subscriber's allotment of 1,000 ordinary shares at GBP 0.01 par value, fully paid, and approves the shareholder subscription agreement; (2) the registered office shall be at Suite 2, 57-63 Line Wall Road, Gibraltar; (3) [Name] is appointed sole director and [Name] company secretary, each severally empowered to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and file statutory returns; (4) the director shall procure the exempt-company certificate, complete Gibraltar Regulatory Authority data-protection registration, and take all ancillary steps for the fitness-app business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies Registry (GFSC) — Name Reservation Desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form NR-1 with three ranked proposed names via the registry portal or through a licensed registered agent. Pay the GBP name-reservation fee. The registrar verifies that names are not identical or confusingly similar to existing Gibraltar or protected UK names. A name reservation is granted for 28 days, renewable once.
required_dossiers: Certified passport copies of each proposed subscriber
Brief statement of intended business objects
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or deferred, the applicant files an amended Form NR-1 with alternative names, or submits a letter of non-objection from the prior registrant to secure consent-based clearance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Signing, and Notarization of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage the licensed registered agent to draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association (M&AA) tailored to an exempted private company limited by shares, including directorial indemnity provisions and share transfer pre-emption rights. Each subscriber executes the M&AA before a notary public; the notary certifies the subscribers' signatures and confirms identity and capacity; the executed documents are returned to the registered agent with the registered office consent letter.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Director (Form CO-02)
Consent to Act as Company Secretary (Form CO-03)
Registered office address consent letter from the agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or agent identifies drafting defects or incompatible clauses, the M&AA is amended by a pre-filing special resolution executed by all subscribers before re-notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form CO-01 together with the notarized M&AA, statutory declarations of compliance, and the registered office nomination through the registered agent's portal or the registry counter. Payment of the incorporation fee is made by BACS, debit card, or agent ledger transfer. The registrar issues a Certificate of Incorporation with the company number upon validation.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Registered office address and consent letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a query or notice of defective filing, the applicant must respond in writing within 14 days, file a revised CO-01 with the clarified object clause, and resubmit the affected schedules; no re-notarization is required unless signatory pages are altered.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Exempted-Status Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies Registry; Income Tax Office, HM Government of Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the Certificate of Incorporation, the registered agent applies for the exempt-company certificate (Form E-1) from the Income Tax Office, submitting a declaration that the company is beneficially owned by non-residents and no Gibraltar-source income is derived beyond approved exempt activities. The tax office records the application and delivers the annual exemption certificate confirming exclusion from Gibraltar income tax.
required_dossiers: Form E-1 (Exempt Company Application) or equivalent
PSC (persons with significant control) register extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Income Tax Office questions economic substance or beneficial ownership, the applicant files supplemental affidavits and a substance narrative (director's meetings in Gibraltar, bank account mandates) to satisfy the local office and secure the exemption certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance Registration and Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Office Agent (Governance Compliance), Gibraltar Companies Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent opens the statutory registers (members, directors, secretaries, PSC, and charges) in physical or approved electronic format, issues share certificates to subscribers, and files the director and secretary appointment forms with the registry. A company minute book is opened, and the agent endorses the corporate seal if adopted by the board.
required_dossiers: Board minutes of the First Board Resolution
Register of Persons with Significant Control
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry rejects an appointment form for non-compliant consent wording, the applicant files a rectified CO-02 within 14 days and, where a statutory deadline is missed, submits a late-filing explanation to mitigate penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Data Protection, Telecom, and Operational Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Regulatory Authority (GRA), Data Protection Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as a data controller/processor under the Data Protection Act 2019 (UK GDPR equivalence) because the fitness app processes biometric health telemetry. Submit the online registration form, pay the annual fee, appoint an EU/UK representative if no establishment exists, and lodge a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) covering biometric data, wearable device integration, and Apple/Google IAP payment flows.
required_dossiers: Privacy policy and biometric-data consent templates
Breach notification procedure and data retention schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the GRA queries the DPIA or consent basis, the company refiles an enhanced DPIA with a lawful-basis assessment, applies pseudonymization measures, and submits an action plan; registration is ultimately granted upon demonstrated compliance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — digital software publishing (NAICS 511210 / ISIC 6201) is not an industrial manufacturing activity; the Gibraltar Regulatory Authority (GRA) E-Commerce Desk provides permissive monitoring only.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Exempt — no industrial or manufacturing operating license required for a software-only health and fitness app tracker; GRA data-processor registration serves as the sole operational permit.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of the Environment and Climate Change, HM Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 — Exempt / Registration Only (no Full EIA Report required; zero point-source emissions from software development and cloud-hosted telemetry services)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or stack-emission thresholds apply. Office-origin waste must comply with the Waste Management Regulations 2020; WEEE (Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment) disposal and RoHS compliance apply to disposed IT/hardware assets; cloud hosting providers must evidence renewable or certified energy usage if publicly marketed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service for the registered office; building structural load and occupancy clearance per Gibraltar Building Regulations (workstation occupancy max 2 persons); portable appliance testing (PAT) for all electrical equipment; first-aid provisioning for the office; and a workplace risk assessment filed with the Health and Safety at Work Unit.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Gibraltar: Income Tax Office, HM Customs and Revenue Department, HM Government of Gibraltar (portal: www.gibraltar.gov.gi/taxation); Bermuda: Accountant General and Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Finance, HM Government of Bermuda (portal: www.gov.bm); United Kingdom (cross-border nexus only): HM Revenue and Customs (portal: www.gov.uk/hmrc).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the Bermuda Exempted Company: incorporate under the Companies Act 1981 with the Bermuda Registrar of Companies, then apply for a Tax Assurance Certificate (TAC) under the Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966, which guarantees exemption from all Bermuda income, capital gains, and withholding taxes through at least 2035. For the Gibraltar presence: register the Bermuda company as a foreign branch under the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 (Cap. 50) with the Gibraltar Companies Registry; obtain the Gibraltar Company Number; and apply to the Gibraltar Income Tax Office, HM Customs and Revenue Department for a Gibraltar Tax Reference Number (TRN). If physical goods are imported, a separate customs registration for the Gibraltar import duty (Prestation) with the Gibraltar Customs Division is required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Bermuda: election to obtain a Tax Assurance Certificate (TAC) under the Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966; election to be designated a non-resident entity for Bermuda Exchange Control purposes, enabling unrestricted foreign currency retention. Gibraltar: no check-the-box regime; the branch may elect profit attribution under the Authorised OECD Approach (AOA) as reflected in the Income Tax Act 2010; group relief elections are available under the Income Tax Act 2010; to the extent the UK anti-avoidance rules are engaged, hybrid mismatch elections under UK CTA 2010 Part 6A may be made to neutralise any structured tax arbitrage.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Gibraltar has no VAT or GST; the only local indirect tax is the Gibraltar Import Duty 'Prestation' (standard flat rate of 8% on most physical imports, with reduced and zero rates for socially important goods). Digital health and fitness app services supplied from Gibraltar are outside the scope of any Gibraltar indirect tax. Cross-border sales to UK and EU consumers are collected and remitted by Apple and Google as deemed suppliers under the marketplace rules: UK VAT at 20% and EU destination-country VAT at applicable standard rates.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GIP/GBP: no turnover threshold applies in Gibraltar for digital services because no VAT/GST exists; the Prestation import duty registration is triggered by the first importation of physical goods, with no de minimis threshold. UK: the deemed-supplier rules require Apple/Google to register and account for UK VAT from the first B2C sale to a UK consumer regardless of the app developer's turnover. EU: the One-Stop-Shop (OSS) special scheme applies to cross-border B2C digital services, with an EUR 10,000 annual intra-EU threshold below which the supplier may charge home-country VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Gibraltar: no statutory e-invoicing, fiscal clearance, or digital stamping mandate; customs declarations are filed electronically through the Gibraltar Customs system. UK: HMRC Making Tax Digital (MTD) mandates digital record-keeping and API-based VAT submission; no real-time invoice clearance is required. EU: Council Directive (EU) 2023/2842 introduces mandatory e-invoicing for intra-EU B2B supplies from 2028, but this does not apply to Gibraltar.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Gibraltar is outside the UK VAT area, so no Gibraltar VAT zero-rating exists and no Gibraltar VAT is chargeable on services. UK zero-rating for exported goods under VAT Act 1994, Schedule 8, Group 7 applies only to supplies made by UK-established suppliers where goods are physically removed from the UK; it does not apply to a Bermuda/Gibraltar app supplier. For B2B cross-border digital supplies, the place of supply is the customer's jurisdiction with the recipient accountable under reverse charge. For B2C supplies through the App Store or Play Store, the marketplace operator is the deemed supplier and must charge and remit UK/EU VAT, while the Bermuda/Gibraltar developer has no substantive VAT registration obligation. Any claim of export/outside-scope treatment must be substantiated with evidence of the customer's establishment, VAT registration numbers where applicable, IP and user-log metadata, and transaction banking records.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Gibraltar Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document) evidencing physical removal
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing export from Gibraltar
Commercial Invoice and underlying export or digital supply contract
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 receipt evidencing foreign exchange repatriation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Deliberate or careless export zero-rating misdeclarations in the UK may trigger retrospective VAT assessments, interest, and penalties of up to 100% of the tax, with criminal prosecution for fraudulent evasion. In Gibraltar, false customs or tax declarations attract penalties up to GIP 5,000 or treble the evaded duty, forfeiture and confiscation of goods and proceeds, and criminal liability under the Customs Tariff Ordinance and the Criminal Code. The Bermuda/Gibraltar group may also face clawback of any refund obtained on the basis of improperly substantiated export documentation, together with professional regulatory sanctions on the advising tax agents.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Government of Gibraltar via the Financial Services Commission (GFSC) in consultation with UK HM Treasury; no independent central bank. Monetary issuance and currency back to the GBP are administered under the Government of Gibraltar's Currency Notes Act. Bank supervision and foreign exchange dealing regulation rest with the GFSC under the Financial Services Act 2019.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Gibraltar pound (GIP) is pegged at 1:1 to the pound sterling (GBP), which circulates interchangeably alongside the GIP. There are no exchange controls applicable to capital or current account transactions for non-resident corporate shareholders. Profit remittance, dividend repatriation, and intercompany loan repayments are freely permitted. Hurdles are limited to standard know-your-customer and anti-money-laundering verification. The offshore Bermuda Exempted Company enjoys non-resident status for FX purposes and no restriction on foreign ownership of accounts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Gibraltar imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio. Exporters and digital service providers may retain receipts in any freely convertible currency (USD, EUR, GBP, GIP). There is no obligation to repatriate or liquidate inbound export proceeds into GIP. The only practical compliance gateway is the provision of a valid economic substance declaration and transaction-level audit trail for tax residence verification.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating is Medium but legally constrained. Gibraltar is not part of the EU/EEA; UK FCA e-money institution authorisation does not passport into Gibraltar. A separate e-money licence from the GFSC is required under the Financial Services Act. Offshore digital EMIs established in the UK, Ireland, or Lithuania may offer ancillary multi-currency IBANs but must not provide core settlement rails without a Gibraltar-authorised agent or holding sub-ledger. For low-risk health fitness app payment flows, a GFSC-licensed EMI acting as a distributive ledger technology payment service provider is viable, but settlement should be anchored through a tier-1 Gibraltar clearing bank to minimise counterparty risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors of the Bermuda Exempted Company must undertake a physical KYC interview at the Gibraltar bank headquarters or at the bank's UK branch if a prior banking relationship exists. Remote onboarding is permitted only with a certified notarised officer identification, apostilled board resolution, and a video conference interview for the beneficial owner. However, the mandatory physical visit of at least one executive director is generally waived only for existing GFSC-regulated corporate clients with verified passport and source-of-wealth documentation. For first-time offshore corporate structures, physical presence of all signing directors is expected.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bermuda Exempted Company with non-resident directors and no visible economic substance in Bermuda
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bermuda Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing, registered office address, register of directors and shareholders, memorandum and articles of association, a full beneficial ownership declaration, and audited or management accounts demonstrating active development of the health fitness app tracker.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-speed cross-border proceeds from suspected digital health subscriptions or stored-value balances
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Third-party audited financial statements, app store payout reports from Apple and Google, merchant platform statements, customer subscription ledgers, a signed client commercial contract, and a clear source-of-funds trail mapping to the underlying consumer transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Debit-side disbursements to software developers, marketing agencies, or overseas payment aggregators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed service agreements, itemised invoices, project milestones, registration of the app's domain and intellectual property, director resolutions approving each payment, and copies of the counterparty's KYC / KYB compliance files.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection from parent or affiliate without obvious tax treatment
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Affiliate loan or share-subscription agreement, board minutes, statutory shareholder register, funding source statements, and a transfer-pricing analysis demonstrating arm's length commercial rationale.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing requires inbound funds to be transmitted via the SWIFT MT103 with OBI (Ordering Bank Information) and a purpose code consistent with 'capital contribution' (e.g., UK purpose code 'FCO' or Gibraltar-specific 'inward equity participation'). The transfer must originate from the shareholder's verified bank account, and the receiving Gibraltar account must be pre-nominated as a capital escrow or operational account. Third-party and crypto-fiat transfers are prohibited. A full documentary package, including the signed injection instrument and the board resolution, must be held in the statutory records. No Gibraltar exchange control authorisation is required, but the bank will require a negative currency control confirmation and anti-money-laundering screening.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements are executed through SWIFT MT103 for cross-border wire payments and MT202 for interbank cover payments where a commercial letter of credit (LC) is used. For EU counterparties and euro-denominated settlements, TARGET-2 and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer are available through the correspondent network. GBP settlements utilise CHAPS and Faster Payments, while USD trade settlements clear through either Fedwire or the Clearing House Interbank Payments System (CHIPS). Gibraltar's clearing rails allow the issuance and confirmation of documentary letters of credit under UCP 600, with stand-by credits under ISP98. For recurring app-payout and intellectual-property licensing fees, the recommended lane is SWIFT MT103 with ACH or SEPA Batch for volume efficiency, subject to an approved disbursement matrix.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forwards (GIP/USD, GBP/USD, EUR/USD) with GFSC-licensed counterparties
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market currencies not freely deliverable in Gibraltar
Cross-Currency Swaps (GBP vs USD and EUR vs USD) with a maturity of up to 12 months
FX Option Contracts (capped collars or zero-premium structures) for downside protection on USD revenue repatriation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar Annual Return of an Overseas Company (Form AR; confirmation of registered office, directors, shareholders and share capital)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the company's annual return date (anniversary of registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monetary penalty of up to GBP 5,000; daily default fines of GBP 50; 12 consecutive months of non-filing may trigger administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Beneficial Ownership Register (BO Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the financial year (e.g., 30 June for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil penalties up to GBP 10,000; director disqualification proceedings and potential restriction of company registrations for persistent default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bermuda Exempted Company Annual Government Fee, Renewal Return and Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the annual renewal date (the anniversary of incorporation of the exempted company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharge; 90 days of unpaid fees can lead to cancellation of the certificate of compliance and strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bermuda Economic Substance Declaration (ESD) Annual Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the close of the relevant financial year (e.g., 30 June for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties up to USD 250,000; false or incomplete declarations may result in loss of tax-exempt status and administrative strike-off.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Flat 10% corporate income tax on assessable profits; territorial basis of taxation (only income accruing in or derived from Gibraltar is chargeable; foreign-source income received in Gibraltar is assessable on a remittance basis for resident companies); no capital gains tax; no VAT; no wealth or turnover taxes; participation exemption applies to qualifying foreign dividends and gains on disposal of non-Gibraltar shareholdings; trading losses may be carried forward indefinitely against future profits of the same trade.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form I (Annual Company Income Tax Return and Computation) filed with the Commissioner of Income Tax; paper filing to the Income Tax Office, Gibraltar, or electronic submission through the official Gibraltar Income Tax e-Services portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on or before 30 November in the relevant Year of Assessment (1 July to 30 June) in respect of the accounting period ended in the preceding Year of Assessment; a company with an accounting period not aligning to the standard cycle may apply in writing to the Commissioner for an extension before the due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section A, Box 1 - Taxpayer Identification (legal name, tax reference number, registration number, registered office)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identifies the Bermudian exempt company and its Gibraltar registration particulars; the tax reference must match the Companies Registry and Beneficial Ownership Register records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State 'non-resident company' if central management and control is outside Gibraltar; attach a letter of representation confirming residence status and the overseas (Bermuda) registration details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section A, Box 2 - Basis and accounting period (start and end dates)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Defines the cycle of profits assessed for the Year of Assessment; entries must reconcile to the audited or management accounts of the health fitness app business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies must apportion the accounting period so that only income attributable to Gibraltar-source activity is returned; foreign periods are excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section B, Box 3 - Gross receipts and business income (Gibraltar-source)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All app subscription revenue, in-app purchase proceeds, telemetry licensing fees and advertising income accruing in or derived from Gibraltar.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Bermuda exempt company that is not tax resident in Gibraltar must include only Gibraltar-sourced digital receipts (e.g. sales contracts performed in Gibraltar or payments sourced to Gibraltar users); all other global app-store turnover is excluded and reconciled in a note.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section B, Box 4 - Deductible expenses, management costs and capital allowances
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costs wholly and exclusively incurred in producing the Box 3 income; depreciation disallowed and replaced by statutory capital allowances on server infrastructure, software development assets and equipment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate shared costs on documented contractual or invoiced arrangements with the parent/licensor; head-office recharges unsupported by transfer pricing documentation are disallowed and trigger adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section C, Box 5 - Net assessable profit/(loss)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 3 less Box 4; the figure to which the 10% rate is applied for the current Year of Assessment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A nil or loss position must be supported by full books and records; losses of a non-resident derived solely from foreign-source income cannot be set off against Gibraltar-source profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section C, Box 6 - Territorial exemptions, participation relief and double tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claims for exclusion of non-Gibraltar-source income, participation exemption on foreign dividends and share gains, and unilateral or treaty credit relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a schedule segregating foreign-source from Gibraltar-source revenue; any claim to a treaty benefit requires a valid foreign tax residence certificate (TRC) and confirmation that the arrangement is not an artificial conduit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section D, Box 7 - Tax charge computation (10%) and tax payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applies the flat 10% rate to the net assessable profit at Box 5 after reliefs at Box 6; final liability is the amount payable or the refund due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If no Gibraltar-source profit exists, enter zero and file a nil return with supporting computation; late filing of a nil return still attracts penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule S-TP1 - Transfer pricing disclosure and controlled transaction schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Discloses cross-border related-party transactions (intercompany app licence fees, management fees, loans, service charges) and the arm's-length method adopted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident filers with controlled transactions exceeding the statutory GIP threshold must complete the schedule and retain the contemporaneous Local File for inspection by the Commissioner.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: fixed penalty of GIP 100, increased by GIP 100 for each month of continued default up to a maximum of GIP 1,000; failure to pay assessed tax on time: interest at the statutory rate plus a late payment surcharge; fraudulent or negligent returns: penalty up to 100% of the tax undercharged, with criminal prosecution available (maximum imprisonment 7 years).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Gibraltar does not impose any withholding tax on dividends, interest or royalties under domestic law, so distributions by or to the Bermuda exempt company are made free of Gibraltar tax at source; where a taxpayer nonetheless seeks formal relief or confirmation under Gibraltar's limited double taxation agreement network (e.g. the Gibraltar-Malta DTA), the administrative protocol is: (1) submit a completed withholding relief application Form R to the Commissioner of Income Tax, (2) provide the counterpart revenue authority's tax residence certificate (TRC) issued within the preceding 12 months, (3) supply the underlying payment flow documentation (dividend resolution, licence agreement, loan agreement), and (4) obtain written advance confirmation of the applicable treatment before the payment is made; TRCs are issued by the Income Tax Office only to entities in good standing on the tax register.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory rate: 0% for royalties and 0% for interest paid by a Gibraltar-resident company to a non-resident recipient; treaty rates under the Gibraltar-Malta DTA are 5% for royalties and 0% for interest (no domestic withholding being imposed, the domestic rate prevails); no withholding is levied on royalty or interest payments routed to a Bermuda exempt company.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: mandatory where annual cross-border controlled transactions exceed GIP 1,000,000; Master File: required where the group's consolidated annual revenue equals or exceeds GIP 850,000,000 (equivalent of EUR 750,000,000 triggering Country-by-Country Reporting); below the threshold, taxpayers must still retain commensurate arm's-length evidence.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Economic Substance (Company) Regulations 2019 apply to every company tax resident in Gibraltar that carries on a 'relevant activity', being banking, insurance, shipping, fund management, financing and leasing, headquarters, distribution and service centres, intellectual property holding, and pure holding-company business. A Bermuda exempt company whose central management and control is exercised in Gibraltar, or that maintains a Gibraltar branch booking app-licensing or distribution income, must demonstrate for each relevant activity: (a) board meetings held in Gibraltar with qualified quorum and minutes recording strategic decisions; (b) an adequate number of full-time employees in Gibraltar proportionate to the app business; (c) adequate operating expenditure in Gibraltar proportionate to the income; and (d) core income-generating activities (software development, data hosting, user tracking, contract negotiation) physically performed in Gibraltar. Pure equity-holding companies enjoy a reduced substance standard requiring only compliance with statutory filing and adequate human resources for holding activity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting Gibraltar-source subscription and in-app purchase receipts from Form I, falsifying the Bermuda exempt company's accounting records, suppressing app-store payout statements, or creating artificial losses to eliminate the 10% tax charge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of the tax undercharged plus statutory interest; civil penalty up to 100% of the under-declared tax; on indictment, an unlimited fine and imprisonment of up to 7 years; confiscation of the proceeds of crime may be ordered by the courts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and controlling officers who sign or approve a false return are jointly and severally liable for civil restitution of the unpaid corporate tax; conviction triggers director disqualification of up to 15 years and a travel ban preventing departure from Gibraltar pending criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the health fitness app tracker through a letterbox arrangement with no physical office, no Gibraltar employees, no effective board meetings in Gibraltar, and no genuine exercise of core income-generating activities in the jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Non-compliance with the Economic Substance (Company) Regulations 2019: financial penalty up to GIP 100,000 for a first offence and up to GIP 300,000 for a repeat offence; continuing default may lead to strike-off of the company by the Companies Registry; any tax advantage derived from the artificial arrangement is reversed with interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly authorise the evasion of substance obligations are disqualified from acting as directors for up to 5 years, are jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate penalties, and may be held personally liable for the company's tax debts where the entity is struck off.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying inflated management fees or excessive app intellectual-property royalties from the Gibraltar operation to the Bermudian parent or UK affiliate to strip the 10% taxed profit pool, or failing to prepare and retain a contemporaneous Local File once the GIP 1,000,000 threshold is crossed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Commissioner may adjust the controlled transaction under the arm's-length principle, re-characterise the arrangement, and raise an assessment on the additional profit at 10%; a penalty of up to 20% of the adjusted tax applies for failure to maintain documentation, and late-payment interest accrues from the original due date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve intercompany pricing without a benchmarking study may be personally liable for penalties attributable to the adjustment; habitually reckless conduct constitutes professional negligence and may result in disqualification orders and civil restitution orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file or keeping inaccurate beneficial ownership data on the Gibraltar Beneficial Ownership Register; failing to file the annual confirmation covering the Bermuda exempt company's Gibraltar registration; concealing the ultimate UK beneficial owner through nominee layers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Failure to file or maintain accurate returns: fine up to GIP 500 per day for continuing default; knowingly or recklessly providing false beneficial ownership information: fine up to GIP 10,000 and/or up to 2 years' imprisonment under the Beneficial Ownership (Access etc.) Act 2017; parallel enforcement action may be taken under the AML (Amendment) Regulations 2019.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the Gibraltar-resident registered agent/nominee are criminally liable; the court may impose travel bans, freeze bank accounts, and issue confiscation orders; a director convicted may be debarred from serving as a director of any Gibraltar company for up to 10 years.
